solutionSql:
SELECT route_id,
       CAST(COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'queued') AS integer) AS queued,
       CAST(COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'in_transit') AS integer) AS in_transit,
       CAST(COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'delivered') AS integer) AS delivered,
       CAST(COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'cancelled') AS integer) AS cancelled,
       CAST(COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'returned') AS integer) AS returned
FROM shipments
GROUP BY route_id
ORDER BY route_id;
notes: Revised text: routes are those that have shipments, which is how the query already worked. Casts: all five count columns cast to integer (were bigint). Sample route 1: queued 14, in_transit 8, delivered 8, cancelled 10, returned 0. The nulls dataset returned every shipment as delivered (20 per route, 0 elsewhere), so that dataset does not separate the status columns.
